subject: Private offer structuring for LogiScale — reseller passback options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marketplace-sales@amazon.com
Cc: procurement@logiscale.com, partner@cloudaxis.io
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer structuring for LogiScale — reseller passback options

Hi team,

Quick context: LogiScale (analytics SaaS) is ready to move forward on a private offer but procurement is asking for a meaningful discount plus a clear reseller passback to CloudAxis (their channel). They want a single private offer that covers both direct commitment pricing and a reseller-retained margin — ideally with as little complexity as possible for their procurement team.

Attached is LogiScale_SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx (requested by CS). Can we confirm what headroom we have on list discounts in AWS private offers and recommended passback percentages for a mid-market account with projected first-year consumption ~$320k? Specific asks:
- Maximum marketplace/PO list discount we can propose for this tier (what AWS will accept).
- Suggested reseller passback % (2 options: aggressive vs conservative).
- Any procurement evidence AWS will require to allow reseller margin to be applied.

Ben/Kim — can you propose a concrete split and I'll loop in CloudAxis & LogiScale procurement once we have a draft?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: LogiScale_SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx
From: marketplace-sales@amazon.com
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, partner@cloudaxis.io
Cc: procurement@logiscale.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer structuring for LogiScale — reseller passback options

Jordan — thanks for the details. A few quick notes from Marketplace:

- Max discount on Private Offers: AWS requires that pricing reflects a legitimate commercial discount, and in our experience public/private combos above ~35% off list trigger additional review. Operationally, discounts in the 20–30% range are straightforward for standard private offers.
- Reseller passback: AWS does support reseller margins but we need a clear chain-of-responsibility and a reseller agreement showing the pass-through. Typical passback guidance we see is 10–18% depending on deal economics and whether the reseller is bringing technical or GTM value.
- Required artifacts: reseller agreement (signed), partner proof-of-capability (partner@cloudaxis.io — case studies or support plan), and the PO justification template filled out by you/LogiScale (we can share the template).

I've attached the PO flow doc (AWS_PO_flow.pdf) that outlines the submission steps and turnaround SLA. If you want, we can do a 20-minute call later this week to walk through the forms; our private-offer team prefers sampled unit pricing per SKU in the submission to speed approval.

Cheers,
Aisha Malik
Marketplace Sales Manager | Amazon Web Services

Attachments: AWS_PO_flow.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@logiscale.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer structuring for LogiScale — reseller passback options

Jordan / Kim — looping in my recommendations after reviewing the SKU matrix and AWS guidance. Quoting AWS here: keep inside ~30% if we want low friction. My recommend split for a smooth close and fair partner economics:

Option A — Conservative (faster approval)
- List discount to LogiScale (private offer): 28% off list
- Reseller passback (CloudAxis): 12% of list (or ~16.7% of our net after discount)
- Rationale: preserves ~60–65% of unit economics for us year-one while giving partner meaningful margin for support/activation.

Option B — Aggressive (requires stronger justification)
- List discount to LogiScale: 34% off list
- Reseller passback: 15% of list
- Rationale: moves needle for procurement; expect AWS review and longer approval. Use only if LogiScale pushes hard on price or if CloudAxis commits to >$40k of enablement spend.

Operational asks:
- Kim, can you draft the reseller evidence packet (partner case study + MSA excerpt) that CloudAxis can sign and we can attach to the AWS PO submission?
- Jordan, I'll prepare PO draft language and a short pricing justification paragraph you can paste into the AWS form.

If we pick Option A, I think we can submit and get approval inside 5–7 business days. Option B could be 2+ weeks with back-and-forth.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Sales | Redwood Inference
